goal: Capture compatible benchmark baseline and prove or reject algorithmic speedup claims.
description: Produce a compatible baseline.json from styio-benchmark or another accepted archive, compare it with benchmark/results/current.json, and keep route-cache, IR-allocation, and scheduler metrics as evidence fields rather than speedup proof by themselves.

acceptance_criteria.text: benchmark/results/baseline.json exists or an accepted external baseline artifact is linked.
python scripts/benchmark-compare.py auto benchmark/results/current.json --baseline-dir benchmark/results --route-cache --ir-alloc --scheduler reports a real baseline/current comparison.
The plan records which original speedup claims are proven, unproven, or rejected by the comparison.

acceptance_criteria.text: Maintainers decide whether full TypeId equality and global SymbolId lookup are required for the current optimization target.

goal: Prove ReadyQueue contention behavior and sanitizer cleanliness before performance claims.
description: The scheduler routes through IReadyQueue and exposes queue kind, but contention reduction and thread-safety claims still need benchmark/profiler and TSan evidence.

acceptance_criteria.text: A contention benchmark or profiler report compares MutexDequeReadyQueue and BoundedMPMCReadyQueue on accepted workloads.
TSan or an accepted concurrency-safety gate passes for the ReadyQueue scheduler path.

goal: Run remote CI and audit validation before declaring algorithm acceptance nightly-ready.
description: The local reports state the fix branch can be pushed for remote validation, but nightly readiness remains blocked until PR or merge-path CI/audit, compatible benchmark evidence, and sanitizer evidence are available.

acceptance_criteria.text: A PR or merge path triggers remote CI and styio-audit for the algorithm acceptance branch.
Remote CI/audit results are linked, passed, or have new failures routed to explicit follow-up checkpoints.
ASan/UBSan and TSan evidence is recorded or explicitly scoped as pending release-lane work.
